cells.tense: A concrete beginning is in your hand now, and you are giving it what it needs.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Choose one part of this growing business you can help with this week, do that help all the way through, and close it out instead of carrying it on.
cells.core:
Something concrete has begun, small enough to hold, and you're feeding it what it needs. You set the conditions and then step back, letting the thing develop at the pace it sets rather than the pace you'd choose. Holding without squeezing is a real skill, and the people near the work can feel how steady that is.

The live question is simply where your strength goes next. You've been the one carrying the whole undertaking, and carrying isn't the same as helping — it keeps you attached to work that could be shared. Pass one piece of it to someone who can hold it, and let that piece end in their hands rather than yours. What you've been steadying will stand for a while by itself, and you get some room back.
cells.sheetLine: You give it what it needs, then keep carrying it.
cells.verb: starting something concrete that must be tended
cells.place: where what is growing is cared for

cells.tense: You will have already known how this growing thing turns out before it has shown you anything.
cells.act: feel the whole of it, all the colours at once
cells.ask: Before the next step with what's growing, sit with everything you already feel about it — all of it together — and hold off moving it forward.
cells.core:
A beginning is here, and you're ahead of it. The thing hasn't shown you what it is, and you've already settled what it will become, how quick, what it needs. From the inside that feels like care. From the other side it feels like being shaped. What's growing isn't free to surprise you.

What's thin isn't restraint. It's letting the feeling arrive fully before you act on it. Sit with what this thing stirs in you, hope and fear at once, and stay until the whole of it has landed. Knowing moves you; rushing moves past you. What you do next, after that, comes from you rather than from the haste.
cells.sheetLine: You've decided how it ends before it's shown you anything.
cells.verb: starting something concrete that must be tended
cells.place: where what is growing is cared for

cells.tense: The beginning came, you did not step in, and you are still standing at that door.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Spread every part of this growing thing where you can see it — the start, the pieces, the worry — and study it until no piece is missing.
cells.core:
Something concrete began and you didn't step into it. The seed sat there, or was set aside, and the steady work of tending it stopped. What's growing waits, quietly. You're good at this kind of care, patient and unforced, and here it's been running low, so nothing moves and nothing closes.

A low tank doesn't need more push. It needs seeing. Spread all of it out: what the thing is, what you did, what you skipped, what you're afraid of. Look at every piece until nothing is hidden. Then the first step isn't a shove. It's just the next clear thing from where you stand now.
cells.sheetLine: It started, and you didn't step in.

cells.tense: You are already giving steady care to something growing, and you would say you aren't.
cells.act: look at the whole of it until nothing is left to see
cells.ask: Look at something you're quietly keeping going, and look at it plain — what it actually needs from you, what you actually give — without dressing any of it up.
cells.core:
There's patient care happening here, and it has no name on it. You'd say the thing is just coming along, or that somebody had to do it. But someone set the conditions, and that someone is you. Your hands are doing this, and your hands don't see themselves doing it.

Stop long enough to see one of these things whole — what it needs, what you hand over, no story laid on top. What you do doesn't shift. Who's doing it does. Care you can see is care you can choose. Care you can't see keeps running underneath like a current.
cells.sheetLine: The steady care here is yours. You'd call it nothing.
